title: The gatekeeper: nothing goes out or runs without passing through you
pitch: A layer that sits in front of any call to an AI model: masks personal data before it goes out, cuts off the call when the day's spending hits the cap, logs every move in a diary that can't be tampered with unnoticed, and stops dead in front of anything with no undo. You plug it into any project of yours by changing one line: where you used to call OpenAI, you now call the gatekeeper.
outcome: An eight-file folder that runs on its own and that you can demo without explaining anything: you run it in front of someone and watch a national ID number and an IBAN disappear from the text going out, watch the system stop cold when you drop the spending cap to zero, watch it call out the exact line number you tampered with in the log, and watch it refuse to send an email until a person types CONFIRM.
time: 4-5 hours the first time. Plugging it into a project you already have, twenty minutes.
requires: Python 3.10 or newer installed. Check by typing python --version in PowerShell: it has to answer with a number.
A text editor for coding. VS Code works and is free.
Knowing how to create a folder and get to it with cd. Nothing else needed: the code is all here and commented.

Optional: an OpenAI account with balance, only if you want to test it against the real model. The whole project works in simulation mode with no key and no cost. The OpenAI API has no free plan and the minimum top-up is $5; with gpt-4o-mini, a thousand queries like the ones in this project cost about €0.02.

structure.what: The configuration template: the variable names, never the values. This one gets shared. Your real copy is called .env and never leaves the computer.
The list of what Git is forbidden from touching: the .env with the key, the log, and the spending counter.
What packages the project uses and at what exact version, so someone else can set up the same thing in a minute.
Finds emails, phone numbers, national IDs, IBANs, and cards inside a text and swaps them for tags before sending it. And puts them back when the answer arrives.
Counts tokens, calculates the cost in euros, keeps the day's running total, and cuts off the call before making it if it doesn't fit the cap.
The chained diary: only appended to at the end, and touching an old line breaks the whole chain in a way that's plainly visible.
Decides which actions have no undo and forces a person to type CONFIRM before running them. If nobody's there, it denies.
The four pieces combined into two functions: pregunta() to talk to the model and ejecuta() to touch the real world. It's the only thing you call from your projects.

steps.title: Set up the folder and the separate box
steps.why: Everything you install for this project has to live inside the project, not scattered across your computer. That's a virtual environment: a sealed box inside the folder. If you want to scrap it tomorrow, delete the folder and nothing else on your system is touched.
steps.code:
# Windows, in PowerShell. The Mac and Linux lines are at the bottom.

mkdir portero
cd portero

# The separate box: only this project's stuff will live inside it.
# If you ever want to scrap it all, delete the folder and nothing else is touched.
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# Three packages and not one more. Every package you install is code
# written by a stranger running with your permissions, so install only what's needed.
#   openai         -> talk to the model (only needed in real mode)
#   python-dotenv  -> read keys from a file, not from the code
#   tiktoken       -> count tokens to know what it'll cost
pip install openai python-dotenv tiktoken

# Write down what you installed and at what exact version.
pip freeze > requirements.txt

# --- Mac and Linux: only these two lines change ---
# python3 -m venv .venv
# source .venv/bin/activate
steps.expected: (.venv) appears in parentheses at the start of the line: that's the sign you're inside the box. pip install finishes with Successfully installed openai-... python-dotenv-... tiktoken-... and the folder ends up with a requirements.txt about twenty lines long.
steps.trouble: On Windows, Activate.ps1 almost always fails the first time with "running scripts is disabled on this system". Type once Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned, answer Y, and activate again. If it's python that fails, "is not recognized as a command", it's not missing: you just didn't check "Add python.exe to PATH" during install. Reopen the same installer, choose Modify, and check it.

steps.title: Keys out of the code and out of Git
steps.why: A key written inside a .py file ends up in Git and from there in GitHub. There are bots crawling GitHub that find an OpenAI key within a minute of you pushing it, and spend it all before you notice. That's why keys live separately, in a .env file Git is forbidden from touching. While you're at it, set the daily spending cap, €1.00, and simulation mode, which lets you test the entire project with no key and no cost.
steps.code:
# Windows, in PowerShell, inside the portero folder with (.venv) showing.
# WATCH OUT for -Encoding ascii: if you put utf8, PowerShell inserts three
# invisible bytes at the start of the file and the FIRST variable in .env stops reading.

# 1. The template that DOES get shared: the names, never the values.
@'
OPENAI_API_KEY=
PORTERO_MODO=simulacion
PORTERO_MODELO=gpt-4o-mini
PORTERO_TOPE_DIARIO_EUR=1.00
PORTERO_MAX_TOKENS_SALIDA=400
PORTERO_SIN_HUMANO=0
'@ | Set-Content .env.example -Encoding ascii

# 2. Your real copy. This one never leaves the computer.
#    In simulation mode you can leave OPENAI_API_KEY empty and spend nothing.
Copy-Item .env.example .env

# 3. What Git is forbidden from touching. .env is first on the list.
@'
.env
.venv/
gasto.json
registro.jsonl
__pycache__/
'@ | Set-Content .gitignore -Encoding ascii

# Check all three are there
dir -Force

# --- Mac and Linux: the same with a heredoc ---
# cat > .env.example << 'FIN'
# OPENAI_API_KEY=
# PORTERO_MODO=simulacion
# PORTERO_MODELO=gpt-4o-mini
# PORTERO_TOPE_DIARIO_EUR=1.00
# PORTERO_MAX_TOKENS_SALIDA=400
# PORTERO_SIN_HUMANO=0
# FIN
# cp .env.example .env
# printf '.env\n.venv/\ngasto.json\nregistro.jsonl\n__pycache__/\n' > .gitignore
steps.expected: dir -Force shows you .env.example, .env, and .gitignore in the folder. If you open .env with Notepad, the first line is OPENAI_API_KEY= with nothing after it, and the fourth line says PORTERO_TOPE_DIARIO_EUR=1.00.
steps.trouble: The mistake that trips up everyone on Windows: type -Encoding utf8 instead of -Encoding ascii and PowerShell inserts three invisible bytes at the start of the file (called a BOM), and the FIRST variable in .env stops reading. The rest do read fine, so you go crazy figuring out why just one fails. Use ascii, as shown in the code above, or create the file from VS Code instead.

steps.title: The redactor: mask personal data before it goes out
steps.why: Before text goes out to the model, anything that identifies a person has to be stripped from it. It's not just caution, it's the GDPR: send a customer's national ID number to a provider with no legal basis for it, and the fine is yours. And the cheapest way to comply is to never send the data at all. Here, each piece of data gets swapped for a tag, the tag gets sent, and when the answer comes back, the real value goes back in. The provider never sees it.
steps.code:
"""
Redactor: finds personal data inside a text and masks it before that text
leaves your computer.

Personal data is anything that lets you identify who's being talked about: an
email, a phone number, a national ID, an IBAN, a card. The idea is simple: we
swap "ana.perez@clinica-sur.es" for "[EMAIL_1]" before sending anything, and
when the answer comes back we put the real value back in. The model's provider
never sees the actual data.
"""

import re

# Each pattern is a search rule written in a language called a "regular
# expression": a short way of saying "find me something shaped like this".
# ORDER MATTERS: longer patterns first, so the phone-number pattern doesn't
# eat three loose chunks of an IBAN.
PATRONES = [
    ("EMAIL", re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}")),
    ("IBAN", re.compile(r"\b[A-Z]{2}\d{2} ?(?:[A-Za-z0-9]{4} ?){3,7}[A-Za-z0-9]{1,4}\b")),
    ("TARJETA", re.compile(r"\b(?:\d{4}[ -]?){3}\d{4}\b")),
    ("DNI", re.compile(r"\b\d{8}[ -]?[A-HJ-NP-TV-Z]\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
    ("NIE", re.compile(r"\b[XYZ][ -]?\d{7}[ -]?[A-HJ-NP-TV-Z]\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
    ("TELEFONO", re.compile(r"\b(?:\+34[ -]?)?[6-9]\d{2}[ -]?\d{3}[ -]?\d{3}\b")),
]


def _nueva_etiqueta(tipo, contador):
    contador[tipo] = contador.get(tipo, 0) + 1
    return "[%s_%d]" % (tipo, contador[tipo])


def redacta(texto, extra=None):
    """
    Returns two things: the masked text and a tag -> real value map.

    'extra' is your list of literals that also need masking: customer names,
    project names, whatever. Proper names can't be caught with a search rule
    without filling everything with false alarms, so that part you provide by hand.
    """
    limpio = texto
    mapa = {}
    contador = {}

    # First your literals, longest to shortest, so "Ana Pérez" gets
    # masked whole and doesn't leave a loose "Pérez" lying around.
    for valor in sorted(set(extra or []), key=len, reverse=True):
        if valor and valor in limpio:
            etiqueta = _nueva_etiqueta("NOMBRE", contador)
            limpio = limpio.replace(valor, etiqueta)
            mapa[etiqueta] = valor

    for tipo, patron in PATRONES:
        vistos = []
        for encontrado in patron.findall(limpio):
            if encontrado not in vistos:
                vistos.append(encontrado)
        for valor in vistos:
            etiqueta = _nueva_etiqueta(tipo, contador)
            limpio = limpio.replace(valor, etiqueta)
            mapa[etiqueta] = valor

    return limpio, mapa


def restaura(texto, mapa):
    """Puts the real values back inside the model's answer."""
    for etiqueta, valor in mapa.items():
        texto = texto.replace(etiqueta, valor)
    return texto


def hay_datos_personales(texto):
    """True if that text still has something unmasked. Used by the log."""
    return bool(redacta(texto)[1])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    prueba = (
        "Reclamación de Ana Pérez, DNI 12345678Z, correo ana.perez@clinica-sur.es, "
        "teléfono 655 123 456. Devolver 340 EUR al IBAN ES91 2100 0418 4502 0005 1332. "
        "Pagó con la tarjeta 4539 1488 0343 6467."
    )
    tapado, mapa = redacta(prueba, extra=["Ana Pérez"])

    print("WHAT LEAVES YOUR COMPUTER:")
    print(tapado)
    print()
    print("Masked data: %d" % len(mapa))
    for etiqueta, valor in mapa.items():
        print("  %-12s -> %s" % (etiqueta, valor))
    print()
    respuesta_del_modelo = "Confirmado el abono a [NOMBRE_1] en la cuenta [IBAN_1]."
    print("ANSWER ALREADY REHYDRATED:")
    print(restaura(respuesta_del_modelo, mapa))
steps.expected: python redactor.py prints the sentence with [NOMBRE_1], [DNI_1], [EMAIL_1], [TELEFONO_1], [IBAN_1], and [TARJETA_1] instead of the data, then "Masked data: 6" with the list of what each one was, and below the rehydrated answer: "Confirmado el abono a Ana Pérez en la cuenta ES91 2100 0418 4502 0005 1332".
steps.trouble: If you get split or partial tags, check the ORDER of the PATRONES list: it's the only delicate part of the file. If the phone pattern runs before the IBAN one, it eats three chunks of the IBAN and leaves the rest loose. Longest to shortest, always. And if a proper name doesn't get masked, that's expected: names can't be caught with a search rule without filling everything with false alarms, that's why they go by hand in the extra list.

steps.title: The counter: how much you've spent today and where the brake is
steps.why: Without a cap, a poorly written loop makes four thousand calls while you have dinner. It's the most repeated story in the industry: you wake up to a €300 bill from a for loop that never stopped. Here what's been spent today gets counted, and the WORST-case cost of the next call gets estimated before making it; if it doesn't fit, it doesn't happen. And watch out: this is a brake you control, inside your code. Also set the hard limit in OpenAI's billing dashboard, which is what saves you the day it's your own code that fails.
steps.code:
"""
Budget: counts what you've spent today and cuts off BEFORE you go over.

A token is the chunk the model splits text into: roughly four letters in
English or Spanish. You pay per token in and per token out, and out costs
more. Two things happen here: estimating the worst-case cost of a call
before making it, and logging the real cost afterward.

The gasto.json file stores the day's running total. New day, starts at zero.
"""

import json
import os
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv

CARPETA = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
load_dotenv(CARPETA / ".env")
FICHERO_GASTO = CARPETA / "gasto.json"

# Public price list, in DOLLARS per million tokens.
# They change every few months: check the provider's pricing page
# before trusting these numbers.
PRECIOS = {
    "gpt-4o-mini": {"entrada": 0.15, "salida": 0.60},
    "gpt-4.1-mini": {"entrada": 0.40, "salida": 1.60},
    "gpt-4o": {"entrada": 2.50, "salida": 10.00},
}
DOLAR_A_EURO = 0.92  # Approximate. Adjust if the exchange rate moves a lot.


class PresupuestoAgotado(Exception):
    """Raised when the call would go over the day's cap."""


def cuenta_tokens(texto, modelo):
    """Counts how many tokens the text splits into."""
    try:
        import tiktoken
        try:
            codificador = tiktoken.encoding_for_model(modelo)
        except KeyError:
            codificador = tiktoken.get_encoding("o200k_base")
        return len(codificador.encode(texto))
    except Exception:
        # The first time, tiktoken downloads its table from the internet. If
        # there's no network, it estimates: a token is roughly 4 characters.
        return max(1, len(texto) // 4)


def coste_euros(modelo, tokens_entrada, tokens_salida):
    """What that amount of tokens costs, in euros."""
    precio = PRECIOS.get(modelo)
    if precio is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "I have no price for '%s'. Add it to PRECIOS before using it. "
            "No price means no cap, and no cap means no protection." % modelo
        )
    dolares = (
        (tokens_entrada / 1_000_000) * precio["entrada"]
        + (tokens_salida / 1_000_000) * precio["salida"]
    )
    return round(dolares * DOLAR_A_EURO, 6)


def tope_diario():
    return float(os.getenv("PORTERO_TOPE_DIARIO_EUR", "1.00"))


def _lee():
    hoy = date.today().isoformat()
    if FICHERO_GASTO.exists():
        datos = json.loads(FICHERO_GASTO.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
        if datos.get("dia") == hoy:
            return datos
    return {"dia": hoy, "gastado_eur": 0.0, "llamadas": 0}


def _escribe(datos):
    FICHERO_GASTO.write_text(
        json.dumps(datos, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8"
    )


def gastado_hoy():
    return _lee()["gastado_eur"]


def comprueba(modelo, texto_entrada, max_tokens_salida):
    """
    Estimates the WORST-case cost of the call (real input + output at
    maximum) and decides whether it can be made. If it doesn't fit the cap, cuts it off.
    """
    entrada = cuenta_tokens(texto_entrada, modelo)
    estimado = coste_euros(modelo, entrada, max_tokens_salida)
    datos = _lee()
    tope = tope_diario()

    if datos["gastado_eur"] + estimado > tope:
        raise PresupuestoAgotado(
            "Blocked. You've spent %.4f EUR today, this call could cost up to "
            "%.4f EUR and the cap is %.2f EUR."
            % (datos["gastado_eur"], estimado, tope)
        )
    return {"tokens_entrada": entrada, "coste_estimado_eur": estimado}


def apunta(modelo, tokens_entrada, tokens_salida):
    """Adds the REAL cost once the call has actually happened."""
    coste = coste_euros(modelo, tokens_entrada, tokens_salida)
    datos = _lee()
    datos["gastado_eur"] = round(datos["gastado_eur"] + coste, 6)
    datos["llamadas"] += 1
    _escribe(datos)
    return coste


if __name__ == "__main__":
    datos = _lee()
    print("Day:        %s" % datos["dia"])
    print("Calls:      %d" % datos["llamadas"])
    print("Spent:      %.4f EUR" % datos["gastado_eur"])
    print("Cap:        %.2f EUR" % tope_diario())
    print("Remaining:  %.4f EUR" % max(0.0, tope_diario() - datos["gastado_eur"]))
    print()
    texto = "Resume esta reclamación en tres líneas." * 20
    tokens = cuenta_tokens(texto, "gpt-4o-mini")
    print("Example: %d input tokens with gpt-4o-mini and 400 output" % tokens)
    print("cost %.5f EUR." % coste_euros("gpt-4o-mini", tokens, 400))
steps.expected: python presupuesto.py gives you today's date, 0 calls, 0.0000 euros spent, the cap at 1.00, and what's left. Below that, an example: 141 input tokens with gpt-4o-mini and 400 output cost 0.00024 euros. Yes, four zeros: that's exactly why you need a counter, because every single call looks free. If you get 195 instead of 141, tiktoken couldn't download its table and used the backup estimate; that's fine too.
steps.trouble: If you get "I have no price for...", that's on purpose. A model not in the PRECIOS table can't be costed, and no cost means no cap. Add it by hand, copying the numbers from the provider's pricing page. Another thing: the first time tiktoken is used it downloads a table from the internet. Without network, you'll see somewhat rounder numbers because it falls back to the four-characters-per-token estimate, approximate but enough to act as a brake.

steps.title: The chained diary: a log that can't be tampered with
steps.why: An editable log proves nothing: if someone can delete the line that incriminates them, the log is decoration. Here each line stores a fingerprint of itself and the previous line's fingerprint, so touching an old line breaks the chain in a way that's plainly visible. It's the same idea as a blockchain, minus the blockchain and the cryptocurrency. And there's a hard rule baked into the code: no personal data ever goes into the log. It records what was done, what it cost, and who asked for it; never the content of the query.
steps.expected: python registro.py answers "OK      The diary is empty: nothing to verify yet." That's correct: nothing's been written yet. The gatekeeper will write to it in step 7.
steps.trouble: If you get ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redactor', you're running it from outside the folder. Python looks for neighboring files from wherever you're standing, not from where the file itself is. cd into the portero folder and run it again.

steps.title: The red button: human approval for the irreversible
steps.why: A program that can send emails and delete files on its own is a ticking bomb. The line you don't cross alone is the irreversible one: sent, deleted, paid, published. There it stops and asks. And not with a "sure? y/n", because by the third time your hand hits the key on autopilot: you have to type CONFIRM in full, while looking at the screen. The most important part of the file is four lines: if nobody's there to answer, the answer is no.
steps.code:
"""
Human approval: nothing irreversible happens without a person typing it in.

Irreversible means it has no undo: an email sent, a file deleted, a payment
made, something published. A "sure? y/n" won't do for that, because by the
third time people click "y" without reading. Here you have to type a full word.

And the golden rule: if nobody's there to answer, the answer is NO.
"""

import os
import re

PALABRA = "CONFIRMO"

# What we consider to have no way back, and why.
IRREVERSIBLES = [
    (re.compile(r"\benvi(ar|o|ando)\b|\bmandar\b", re.I),
     "goes out to another person and there's no un-sending it"),
    (re.compile(r"\b(borrar|eliminar|vaciar|purgar|archivar)\b", re.I),
     "destroys data"),
    (re.compile(r"\b(pagar|cobrar|transferir|reembolsar|facturar|suscribir)\b", re.I),
     "moves money"),
    (re.compile(r"\b(publicar|desplegar|deploy|postear|tuitear)\b", re.I),
     "outside people will see it"),
    (re.compile(r"\b(drop|delete|truncate|alter)\b", re.I),
     "touches the database and there's no trash can there"),
    (re.compile(r"push\s+--force|rm\s+-rf|shutdown|format", re.I),
     "has no undo"),
]


class Denegado(Exception):
    """Raised when the human says no, or when there's no human."""


def motivo_irreversible(accion):
    """Returns the reason if the action is irreversible, or None if it isn't."""
    for patron, motivo in IRREVERSIBLES:
        if patron.search(accion):
            return motivo
    return None


def pide_permiso(accion, detalle, coste_eur=None):
    """
    Returns a dict with the decision. Doesn't run anything: only decides.
    """
    motivo = motivo_irreversible(accion)

    if motivo is None:
        return {"aprobado": True, "modo": "not-needed", "motivo": None}

    # No human present (a scheduled overnight task, a server) means nothing
    # gets approved. Denying by default is what prevents nasty surprises.
    if os.getenv("PORTERO_SIN_HUMANO", "0") == "1":
        return {"aprobado": False, "modo": "no-human", "motivo": motivo}

    print()
    print("=" * 62)
    print("  STOP. This cannot be undone.")
    print("=" * 62)
    print("  Action : %s" % accion)
    print("  Reason : %s" % motivo)
    print("  Detail : %s" % detalle)
    if coste_eur is not None:
        print("  Cost   : %.4f EUR" % coste_eur)
    print("=" * 62)

    try:
        escrito = input("Type %s to authorize (anything else cancels it): " % PALABRA).strip()
    except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
        # Not even a keyboard present. Not a yes.
        escrito = ""

    aprobado = escrito == PALABRA
    print("Authorized." if aprobado else "Cancelled. Nothing was done.")
    return {"aprobado": aprobado, "modo": "human", "motivo": motivo}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ejemplos = [
        "guardar borrador en la carpeta de plantillas",
        "enviar correo al cliente",
        "delete from clientes where id = 42",
        "resumir el informe trimestral",
        "transferir 340 EUR de reembolso",
    ]
    for accion in ejemplos:
        motivo = motivo_irreversible(accion)
        print("%-45s %s" % (accion, ("ASKS FOR PERMISSION: " + motivo) if motivo else "goes through on its own"))
steps.expected: python aprobacion.py prints a table of five examples. "guardar borrador en la carpeta de plantillas" and "resumir el informe trimestral" go through on their own. "enviar correo al cliente", "delete from clientes where id = 42", and "transferir 340 EUR de reembolso" ask for permission, each with its reason written next to it.
steps.trouble: If one of your actions doesn't trigger the warning, its keyword isn't in the IRREVERSIBLES list. Add it. And always err on the paranoid side: asking too often costs you ten annoying seconds; not asking when it should have costs an email sent to 400 customers that can't be unsent.

steps.title: The gatekeeper: the four pieces in two functions
steps.why: The four pieces on their own protect nothing. They protect when they're the only path through. From here on, in your projects you no longer call OpenAI directly: you call pregunta(). Notice the order inside that function, because it's the only thing that truly matters: mask first, then check the budget, then call, then log the spend and the record. Change that order and the protection becomes decoration.
steps.code:
"""
The gatekeeper: the only door your calls to the model and your actions on
the real world pass through.

There's no new logic here. This combines the four pieces into two functions:

  pregunta(...)  -> masks data, checks the budget, calls, logs cost and record
  ejecuta(...)   -> checks if it's irreversible, asks permission, logs, runs

From now on, in your projects you don't call OpenAI: you call the gatekeeper.
"""

import os
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv

import aprobacion
import presupuesto
import registro
from redactor import redacta, restaura

CARPETA = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
load_dotenv(CARPETA / ".env")

MODO = os.getenv("PORTERO_MODO", "simulacion")
MODELO = os.getenv("PORTERO_MODELO", "gpt-4o-mini")
MAX_SALIDA = int(os.getenv("PORTERO_MAX_TOKENS_SALIDA", "400"))


def _llama_al_modelo(texto, modelo, max_salida):
    """
    Talks to OpenAI. In simulation mode nothing leaves the computer and
    nothing gets spent: good for testing all four protections for free.
    """
    if MODO != "real":
        respuesta = (
            "[SIMULATION] I received %d already-cleaned characters. "
            "I haven't called anyone and you haven't spent anything." % len(texto)
        )
        return respuesta, presupuesto.cuenta_tokens(respuesta, modelo)

    from openai import OpenAI

    clave = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")
    if not clave:
        raise RuntimeError("Missing OPENAI_API_KEY in the .env file.")

    cliente = OpenAI(api_key=clave)
    completado = cliente.chat.completions.create(
        model=modelo,
        max_tokens=max_salida,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": texto}],
    )
    return completado.choices[0].message.content, completado.usage.completion_tokens


def pregunta(texto, usuario="anonymous", nombres=None, modelo=MODELO):
    """
    Sends a query to the model with all four protections in place.
    May raise PresupuestoAgotado. That means it worked.
    """
    limpio, mapa = redacta(texto, extra=nombres)
    aviso = presupuesto.comprueba(modelo, limpio, MAX_SALIDA)

    respuesta_limpia, tokens_salida = _llama_al_modelo(limpio, modelo, MAX_SALIDA)
    coste = presupuesto.apunta(modelo, aviso["tokens_entrada"], tokens_salida)

    registro.apunta({
        "tipo": "consulta",
        "usuario": usuario,
        "modo": MODO,
        "modelo": modelo,
        "datos_tapados": len(mapa),
        "etiquetas": sorted(mapa.keys()),
        "tokens_entrada": aviso["tokens_entrada"],
        "tokens_salida": tokens_salida,
        "coste_eur": coste,
        "acumulado_dia_eur": presupuesto.gastado_hoy(),
    })

    return restaura(respuesta_limpia, mapa)


def ejecuta(accion, detalle, hazlo, usuario="anonymous"):
    """
    Runs something in the real world. If it has no undo, stops and asks.
    'hazlo' is a no-argument function: only called if permission is granted.
    """
    veredicto = aprobacion.pide_permiso(accion, detalle)

    accion_limpia, _ = redacta(accion)
    detalle_limpio, _ = redacta(detalle)

    registro.apunta({
        "tipo": "accion",
        "usuario": usuario,
        "accion": accion_limpia,
        "detalle": detalle_limpio,
        "aprobado": veredicto["aprobado"],
        "decision": veredicto["modo"],
        "motivo": veredicto["motivo"] or "",
    })

    if not veredicto["aprobado"]:
        raise aprobacion.Denegado("'%s' was not executed." % accion_limpia)
    return hazlo()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Mode: %s | Daily cap: %.2f EUR | Spent today: %.4f EUR"
          % (MODO, presupuesto.tope_diario(), presupuesto.gastado_hoy()))

    caso = (
        "Redacta la respuesta a esta reclamación. Cliente: Ana Pérez, "
        "DNI 12345678Z, ana.perez@clinica-sur.es, teléfono 655 123 456. "
        "Pide el reembolso de 340 EUR al IBAN ES91 2100 0418 4502 0005 1332."
    )

    print("\n--- 1. Query with personal data inside ---")
    try:
        print(pregunta(caso, usuario="support", nombres=["Ana Pérez"]))
    except presupuesto.PresupuestoAgotado as error:
        print("BUDGET: %s" % error)

    print("\n--- 2. Reversible action: goes through on its own ---")
    print(ejecuta("guardar borrador", "Se queda en la carpeta de plantillas",
                  lambda: "Draft saved.", usuario="support"))

    print("\n--- 3. Irreversible action: this is where it stops and asks ---")
    try:
        print(ejecuta("enviar correo al cliente",
                      "Para: ana.perez@clinica-sur.es | Asunto: Reembolso aprobado",
                      lambda: "Email sent.", usuario="support"))
    except aprobacion.Denegado as error:
        print("DENIED: %s" % error)

    print("\n--- 4. The diary, verified end to end ---")
    correcto, mensaje = registro.verifica()
    print(("OK: " if correcto else "ALARM: ") + mensaje)
steps.expected: python portero.py does four things in a row. The first returns a simulated answer and spends nothing. The second saves a draft without asking. The third stops in a box that reads "STOP. This cannot be undone.", with the action, the reason, and the detail, and waits: type CONFIRM and out comes "Email sent", type anything else and out comes "Cancelled". The fourth finishes with "OK: 3 lines verified. The chain is intact."
steps.trouble: If the first test answers "BUDGET: Blocked..." with the cap at 1.00 euro, check gasto.json: you've used up your allowance from testing so much. Delete that file or raise PORTERO_TOPE_DIARIO_EUR in .env. If you get RuntimeError: Missing OPENAI_API_KEY, you set PORTERO_MODO=real without a key; leave it as simulacion until you actually want to spend money.

steps.title: Break it on purpose: the four doors, tested
steps.why: A protection you've never watched trip isn't a protection, it's an assumption. Here you force all four: try to spend with the cap at zero, leave the system with no human present, search for the customer's email inside the log, and forge a diary line by hand. This is what you show off in an interview, and it's what separates "I built a security project" from "I proved my security project works".
steps.code:
# Windows, in PowerShell, inside the portero folder.

# --- 1. The diary, as it stands ---
python registro.py

# --- 2. The cap cuts off. A variable set here overrides .env,
#        so you can test without touching the file.
$env:PORTERO_SIN_HUMANO="1"
$env:PORTERO_TOPE_DIARIO_EUR="0"
python portero.py

# --- 3. With no human present, the irreversible action denies itself ---
#        (you just saw this in the test above: "DENIED")
Remove-Item Env:PORTERO_TOPE_DIARIO_EUR
python portero.py
Remove-Item Env:PORTERO_SIN_HUMANO

# --- 4. The customer's email CANNOT be in the log ---
Select-String -Path registro.jsonl -Pattern "ana.perez@"   # nothing should show up
Select-String -Path registro.jsonl -Pattern "EMAIL_1"      # this does show up

# --- 5. Forge the diary by hand and watch it trip ---
#        Open the file, change "support" to "intern" on any line,
#        save as plain UTF-8, and close.
notepad registro.jsonl
python registro.py

# --- 6. Reset it clean again (in a real system this step does NOT exist) ---
Remove-Item registro.jsonl, gasto.json
python portero.py

# --- Mac and Linux ---
# PORTERO_SIN_HUMANO=1 PORTERO_TOPE_DIARIO_EUR=0 python portero.py
# PORTERO_SIN_HUMANO=1 python portero.py
# grep "ana.perez@" registro.jsonl ; grep "EMAIL_1" registro.jsonl
# nano registro.jsonl   (on Mac: open -e registro.jsonl)
# rm registro.jsonl gasto.json
steps.expected: In test 2 you get "Blocked. You've spent 0.0000 EUR today, this call could cost up to 0.0002 EUR and the cap is 0.00 EUR." In test 3, "DENIED" without asking you anything. In test 4, the first search finds nothing and the second finds EMAIL_1. In test 5, after touching the file, "ALARM   Line 2: content doesn't match its fingerprint. Someone edited this line.", with the number of the line you actually changed.
steps.trouble: Once the diary is forged, the alarm stays tripped forever: the chain is broken and there's no way to patch it. That's exactly what's supposed to happen. To start over you have to delete registro.jsonl, and that deletion is irreversible: it wipes the entire history. In a real system that option doesn't exist, because the log is stored somewhere your own program has permission to append to but not to delete.

checks: You run python redactor.py and the sentence that comes out has no email, no national ID, no IBAN, no card left in it: only tags. And the line below has the real values again, because rehydration also works.

You open registro.jsonl and search for the customer's email. It doesn't appear. [EMAIL_1] appears. If the whole email shows up, you've changed the order inside pregunta() and you're logging before masking.
You set PORTERO_TOPE_DIARIO_EUR to 0 and python portero.py refuses to call the model, telling you in the same message how much you've spent, how much the call would cost, and where the cap is.
You change any word inside registro.jsonl, save, and python registro.py calls out the exact line number that was tampered with and exits with an error.
With PORTERO_SIN_HUMANO=1, the send-email action denies itself, no questions asked. Without that variable, the program stops and doesn't continue until someone types CONFIRM in full.
You run git status inside the folder and it doesn't mention .env, gasto.json, or registro.jsonl. If it mentions them, .gitignore is written wrong or you left it in the wrong folder.
extend: Add your own patterns to the redactor: license numbers, license plates, policy numbers, cadastral references, medical record numbers. A new pattern is two lines in the PATRONES list. Test each one against a real case before trusting it, because a badly written rule under-masks and doesn't warn you at all.

Swap the single daily cap for a per-person cap: instead of a gasto.json with one number, a dictionary with each user's spending. That way the intern gets €0.50 a day and the billing system gets €20. With that you can start charging for use of your tool, because you know exactly what each person consumes.

Take the log off the disk. As long as the diary is a file next to the code, whoever can run the program can delete it, and then it's worthless as proof. Send it to a database where your program has permission to insert but not to modify or delete (in Postgres that's a GRANT INSERT with no UPDATE or DELETE). That's the leap from "course project" to "something I can defend in an audit".
defend: "If the model can't see the national ID or the name, doesn't the answer come out crippled?" — Almost never, and it's checkable in two minutes. When you ask it to draft a refund letter, the model doesn't care whether the customer is called Ana Pérez or [NOMBRE_1]: the job is the text's structure, not the data. It breaks when the task depends on the data itself, like validating whether a national ID checksum is correct or figuring out which bank an IBAN belongs to. And that's exactly the right answer: those things don't get sent to the model, they're done in your own code with a twenty-line function that's always right and costs zero.

"Why chain fingerprints instead of just writing the log and calling it done?" — Because an editable log proves nothing: anyone with access to the file can delete the line about the error that cost €200. With the chain, touching an old line throws off every line below it and registro.py gives you the exact number. And it's worth being honest here, which is what an interview appreciates: whoever has write access to the file can recompute the whole chain. This doesn't stop an attacker with disk access; it stops carelessness and quick edits, which is ninety-nine percent of real cases. For the other one percent, the log gets sent somewhere your program can only append to.

"Why make people type a whole word instead of a yes or no?" — Because a yes or no gets clicked without reading. By the fifth time the prompt shows up, the hand hits the key on autopilot. Typing CONFIRM forces you to actually look at the screen, and on that screen is what's about to happen: what action, on what, and why it has no undo. The second half of the answer is the part that matters: if nobody answers, it gets denied. A program running at 3am, with nobody watching, shouldn't be able to send a single email.
